Nikhilesh Dutta, Deputy Attorney-General, with Md Laikuzzaman, Assistant Attorney-General and ANM Gaziul Huq, Abdul Mannan Khan, Advocates --- For the Opposite Party.
parties:
Sohali Thakur and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
State, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment:
AK Badrul Huq J: By this application under section 526 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the accused-petitioners seek transfer of a Session case from the Sessions Division of Dhaka to any other court of competent jurisdiction to another Sessions Division around Dhaka whereupon Rule was issued calling upon the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka to show cause as to why the proceeding of Session Case No. 633 of 1996 pending in the court of Third Additional Sessions Judge, Dhaka should not be transferred to any other court of competent jurisdiction of another Sessions Division around Dhaka or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 i) The accused-petitioners being unable to defend them due to non-observance of the required procedure as per law by the court of Sessions Judge, Dhaka and Third Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Dhaka and their attitude shown in the case, a genuine apprehension had grown in the minds of the accused-petitioners that they would be deprived of adequate opportunity for defending them and the trial would not be fair, free and in accordance with law in the court of Decisions Judge, Dhaka and also in the Third Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Dhaka. 

 ii) The atmosphere in the court indicates that there exists real bias in the mind of the judge against the accused persons including the accused-petitioners and, therefore, the Session Case No.633 of 1996 ought to be transferred to any other come tent Sessions Court of any other Sessions Division around Dhaka. 

 3. Before adverting to the grounds so formulated it civil be profitable to notice the relevant provision of law on transfer contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure. The High Court Division''s power to transfer a case is embodied in section 526 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Section 526(1)(a) provides that whenever it is made to appear to the High Court Division that a fair and impartial inquiry or trial cannot be held in any Criminal Court subordinate thereto, the High Court Division can pass order transferring any case to any other court subordinate to it. Section 561(1)(e) enjoins that the High Court Division can transfer a case if it appears that the transfer is necessary to secure the ends of justice. 

 5. The law of conferring powers on the High Court Division to transfer a case from one court to another is based on the susceptibilities of the litigant public and derives its origin from the maxim that justice should not only be done, but also should be publicly recognized as having been done. The object is to sustain public confidence in Judicial Courts/Tribunals, and to root out any suspicion, or distrust from the minds of the litigant public. Section 526 of the Code does not make it absolutely necessary that there should be a reasonable apprehension in the mind of the accused that he will not get a fair and impartial trial. It is enough if it appears from the circumstances placed before the High Court Division that a fair and impartial trial cannot be had in that court. The result is that the High Court Division may transfer a case from one court to another if it is made to appear to it that the accused cannot have a fair or impartial trial in that court and also where circumstances have so transpired as to lead the accused to entertain a reasonable apprehension that he may not have a fair and impartial trial. But it must be borne in mind that it is not sufficient for the applicant merely to allege that he will not get an impartial trial before the court in which the case is pending. He must place before the High Court Division facts which give rise to such apprehension and the High Court Division should not pass an order of transfer unless it is satisfied on the facts disclosed in the application that there arises a reasonable apprehension that he will not have a fair and impartial trial. It cannot be at all said that taking trouble of making a transfer application is itself proof of existence of reasonable apprehension in the mind of the applicant that he would not get a fair trial. 

 6. Bearing the above principles in mind we have to approach the controversy in the present case i.e. whether there is any basis or foundation for the apprehension on the part of the accused-petitioners that they may not get fair and impartial trial in the court where the case is pending and whether to secure the ends of justice, the case is required to be transferred. 

 a) The accused-petitioners and accused Faruk Thakur stand charged under sections 302/149 of the Penal Code in Session Case No.633 of 1996 which arose out of Gulshan PS Case No.19(1)96 under sections 448/323/302/114 of the Penal Code. They faced trial before the learned Sessions Judge, Dhaka and now facing trial before the Third Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Dhaka. 

 b) The prosecution case is that, on 7-1-1996 at 10-00 PM accused Faruk Thakur along with 20/25 persons trespassed into the house plot No. 3A Gulshah Residential Area and carried on a reign of terror. The victim Shamsul Alam who was alleged to be a tenant of one Mujibur Rahman, the alleged owner of that house, accompanied with his men went to the said house. There had been indiscriminate shootings. At certain stage, accused Faruk Thakur with his firearm shot at Shamsul Alam who was declared dead by the doctors on duty in the Dhaka Medical College Hospital where he was taken after the alleged occurrence. In the First Information Report only accused Faruk Thakur had been named. 

 ii. The learned Sessions Judge, Dhaka received the case record for trial on 4-11-96. The learned Sessions Judge framed charge against the accused-petitioners and accused Faruk Thakur on 27-11-1996 under sections 302/149 of the Penal Code. 

 v. On 8-2-1998 the accused-petitioner Nos. 1-7, 9 and 11 were present in the court by filing Hajira and the accused-petitioner No. 8 prayed for time for his presence in the court on the next date on medical ground. The accused-petitioner No. 10 was in jail custody in connection with another criminal case instituted against him and a prayer for time had been presented on his behalf for his presence on the next date. The learned Sessions Judge cancelled the bail of all the accused-petitioners taking the view that they misused the privilege of bail granted to them and they created obstruction in the trial. 

 vi. On 12-2-1998 the accused-petitioner Nos.8 and 10 surrendered before the court and prayed for bail. Bail application had been also presented for the rest accused-petitioners i.e., accused-petitioner Nos.1-7, 9 and 11. The prayer for bail of the accused-petitioners stood rejected by the learned Sessions Judge by his order dated 12-2-1998. Thereafter, the accused-petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 were enlarged on ad-interim bail with reference to a Criminal Miscellaneous case pending in the High Court Division. The other accused-petitioners were also, subsequently, enlarged on bail by the learned Sessions Judge on 1-3-1998. 

 vii. On 5-3-1998 an application was presented before the learned Sessions Judge for transfer of the case to any other court of competent jurisdiction under his Sessions Division. The application was taken up for hearing on 19-3-1998 and the same stood rejected. The learned Sessions Judge in rejecting the said transfer application took the view that trial could not be concluded due to his engagement in the court and taking into consideration of his future engagement in the court himself transferred the case to the Third Court of Additional Sessions Judge. 

 viii. The learned Additional Sessions Judge received the case record on the same date i.e., on 19-3-1998. The accused-petitioners on the said date surrendered before the transferee court, i.e. Third Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Dhaka with a prayer for bail. The learned Additional Sessions Judge refused to grant them bail, cancelled the bail granted by the learned Sessions Judge and sent them to custody taking the view that the evidences of 14 witnesses had been recorded and only a junior Advocate had been present in the court and the other three senior Advocates were absent and the accused-petitioners resorted to tactics to delay the conclusion of the trial. 

 8. Viewed in the perspective of the foregoing discourse it manifests that the learned Sessions Judge due to absence of the two accused-persons namely, the accused-petitioner Nos. 8 and 10 cancelled the bail of all the accused-petitioners i.e. the accused-petitioner Nos. 1-7, 9 and 11 who were very much present in the court by filing hajira. Out of the said two accused persons accused-petitioner No.10 was in jail custody in connection with another criminal case instituted against him and the accused-petitioner No.8 faced an accident and the application for time was on medical ground. There cannot be any logic on the part of the learned Sessions Judge to cancel the bail of the other accused-petitioners who were very much present in the court by filing hazira merely because the other two accused-petitioners were absent by filing application through their Lawyers for their presence on the next date. It reveals, further, that the learned Sessions Judge himself was of the view that because of his engagement he was not in a position to conclude the trial and in future also the court would be engaged. But it is curious enough to notice here that he rejected the application filed by the accused-petitioners for transfer of the case but at the same time transferred the same for the conclusion of the trial to the Third Court of Additional Sessions Judge. 

 9. Let us now direct our attention to the transferee Judge who is the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Third Court, Dhaka. The accused-petitioners were on bail granted by the learned Session Judge when the case was transferred by him to the Third Court of Additional Sessions Judge. On 19-3-1998 there had been no materials before the learned Additional Sessions Judge which prompted him to cancel the bail of the accused-petitioners. As a transferee court before it there had been no allegation of any type against the accused-petitioners even at the instance of the State. As a practice, the transferee court on receipt of the case record allows the accused persons to continue on the same bail granted by the transferor court and in the instant case the transferor court is no other than the court of Session itself. It is emphasized that once bail is granted by a court of competent jurisdiction then strong and exceptional grounds would be required for cancellation thereof. 

 10. The learned Deputy Attorney-General having been confronted with the peculiar circumstances and materials on record found it difficult to resist the application. He with all fairness submitted that to secure the ends of justice this case may be transferred to any other court of competent jurisdiction of any other Sessions Division around Dhaka. 

 11. The facts, circumstances and materials brought on record undoubtedly lead to a suggestion that the apprehension in the minds of the accused-petitioners that they will not get fair and impartial trial and treatment in the hands of the Additional Sessions Judge or any other Judge of the Sessions Division of Dhaka has got a basis and the apprehension cannot be ruled out. In resolving the subject matter of controversy ie transfer'' we are to keep in view the centuries old maxim "Justice should not only be done, but should manifestly and undoubtedly be seen to be done". The proposition of law on the subject has been laid down in the case of Serjeant vs Dale (1877) 2 Queen Bench Division and Rex vs. Sussex Justices (1924)1 King Bench Division. The propositions deducible are these. 

 "The transfer of a case from a court of competent jurisdiction is justified only if there is a reasonable apprehension in the mind of the party concerned that the Court would not be able to act fairly and impartially in the matter." 

 12. Keeping in view the entire picture presented before us we are of the considered view that since there is an apprehension in the mind of the accused-petitioners in the matter of getting fair and impartial trial in the hands of any Sessions Judge under the Sessions Division, Dhaka and also since they lost confidence, the case is required to be transferred from the Sessions Division, Dhaka to any other Sessions Judge of any other Sessions Division around Dhaka. 

 13. The Sessions Division of Narsingdi is around Dhaka and it will be convenient for both the parties if the case is transferred to the said Sessions Division and trial is concluded there. 

 14. Mr Khondker Mahbub Hossain and Mrs Farida Khan, learned Advocates for the accused-petitioners, Mr Nikhilesh Dutta, learned Deputy Attorney-General, Mr A N Md Gaziul Huq and Mr Abdul Mannan Khan, learned Advocates for the State also agreed to the transfer of the case to any other Sessions Judge of the Sessions Division of Narsingdi. 

 15. In the result, this Rule succeeds and the same is, accordingly, made absolute. The Session Case No.633 of 1996 pending in the Third Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Dhaka under the Sessions Division of Dhaka be transferred to the Court of learned Sessions Judge, Narsingdi under the Sessions Division of Narsingdi. The learned Sessions Judge, Narsingdi will issue proper notices to the accused-petitioners and also to the Deputy Commissioner, Narsingdi intimating the date of the trial. But in case if the learned Sessions Judge, Narsingdi is too busy, the case can be transferred by him to some other Additional Sessions Judge for trial and disposal in accordance with law.
